findings.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:87 — Local cache is set before CreateOrUpdateDevice, so a device rejected with ErrDeviceLimitReached hits the cache on its next request within 29 minutes, TagDevice returns nil, and it is authenticated, which means a page refresh bypasses the limit.

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:115 — Device IDs come from a client-controlled header, so one unauthenticated client can send N random X-Grafana-Device-Id values to fill the limit and lock every new legitimate anonymous user out for up to 30 days (cascade DoS).

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:120 — Requests with no device-ID header (or an unparseable remote address) return nil before any limit check, so any API or script client that omits the header gets unlimited anonymous access and the limit only binds the cooperating frontend.

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44 — Tagging now runs synchronously in Authenticate on the request context and adds a COUNT(*) plus a write on every cache miss, so a flood of unique device IDs turns into amplified DB load, and a slow DB directly adds latency to every new anonymous request.

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database_test.go:51 — TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only checks that a new device is rejected; it never checks that an existing device can still update at the limit, or that a rejected device stays rejected on retry through TagDevice/cache, so the cache bypass passes green.

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:110 — The count-then-insert is not atomic (TOCTOU), so concurrent first requests from new devices across goroutines or HA instances can all see count < limit and insert, going past the configured limit.

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:111 — If CountDevices fails (DB outage), the error is logged and authentication succeeds, and because the cache is already set that device skips enforcement for 29 minutes, so the limit fails open silently during DB degradation.

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:52 — ProvideAnonDBStore gains an unbound int64 param and the AnonStore wire binding is no longer consumed, yet pkg/server/wire.go (and generated wire_gen/enterprise wireexts) are not updated in the diff, so the DI graph will fail to generate or leave a dangling provider.

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:37 — ProvideAnonymousDeviceService now takes db.DB and builds its store internally, which breaks any external caller or enterprise binding that injects anonstore.AnonStore and removes the ability to substitute the store.
pkg/setting/setting.go:1654 — New config key [auth.anonymous] device_limit is not added to conf/defaults.ini, conf/sample.ini, or the configuration docs, so operators cannot discover it.

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:45 — Authenticate now returns a plain fmt.Errorf ErrDeviceLimitReached (not an errutil error), so anonymous clients over the limit get a generic auth failure with no stable status or message ID.

packages/grafana-data/src/types/config.ts:200 — TS type declares anonymousDeviceLimit as number or undefined, but the Go DTO is a non-pointer int64 without omitempty, so the backend always sends a number (0 meaning unlimited) and undefined never occurs.

packages/grafana-runtime/src/config.ts:97 — Without a type annotation, `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined` narrows the GrafanaBootConfig property to type undefined under strict mode, so consumers can't read it as a number.

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:87 — Device key is cached before CreateOrUpdateDevice runs, so after a new device gets ErrDeviceLimitReached, its next requests within 29 minutes hit the cache, TagDevice returns nil, and anonymous auth succeeds, bypassing the limit

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:110 — The count-then-insert check is not atomic, so concurrent first requests from new devices (or from several HA instances) can all see count < limit and insert, pushing the device count past device_limit

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44 — The limit only applies when an X-Grafana-Device-Id header is present (TagDevice returns nil without it), so any client that leaves the header out is authenticated anonymously no matter what device_limit is set to

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:52 — ProvideAnonDBStore now requires a bare int64 while ProvideAnonymousDeviceService takes db.DB instead of AnonStore, so any existing wire provider/binding for ProvideAnonDBStore/AnonStore (e.g. pkg/server/wire.go, not changed in this diff) will fail wire generation or leave a second, unlimited store

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:95 — On MySQL, RowsAffected counts changed rows rather than matched rows, so updating an existing device with the same IP, user agent and second-precision updated_at returns 0 and wrongly fails with ErrDeviceLimitReached

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:110 — Every device upsert with device_limit>0 first runs an uncached COUNT(*) over the 30-day updated_at range; the cost grows with active device count (range scan up to the limit) and is repeated for every new or client-spoofed X-Grafana-Device-Id cache miss, even though the result could be cached or maintained cheaply.

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44 — Device tagging moved from a background goroutine into the synchronous Authenticate path, so each anonymous request that misses the local cache now waits on 1-3 DB round-trips (COUNT, upsert/UPDATE), even when device_limit is 0, and a slow DB now delays authentication directly.

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:87 — Cache key is set before CreateOrUpdateDevice, so after a device is rejected with ErrDeviceLimitReached every later request within 29m hits the cache, returns nil, and authenticates, making the limit enforceable only on the first request

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:87 — Now that the write uses the request ctx, a client disconnect or transient DB error leaves the device unrecorded while the pre-set cache entry suppresses any retry for 29m, undercounting devices

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44 — Tagging now runs synchronously in Authenticate with the request ctx and no timeout (the old 2m bounded detached ctx is gone), so a slow or unavailable DB adds COUNT+write latency or stalls anonymous requests

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:110 — Count-then-insert is not atomic (no transaction/lock), so concurrent new devices across requests/instances can each see count<limit and exceed the configured device limit

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:95 — rowsAffected==0 is treated as limit reached, but MySQL reports 0 affected rows when the UPDATE changes nothing (same-second updated_at, same IP/UA), so a legitimately registered device can be rejected

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:87 — Device key is cached before CreateOrUpdateDevice runs, so after an ErrDeviceLimitReached rejection the same device ID gets through on any retry within 29 minutes (cache hit returns nil), which means the limit only blocks the first request

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:120 — A request that leaves out the client-controlled X-Grafana-Device-Id header, or has an unparseable remote address (line 128), returns nil before the limit check and still gets anonymous access, so curl or API clients bypass the device limit completely

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:115 — An unauthenticated attacker can send requests with random device IDs (no rate limiting or verification) to fill device_limit, locking every legitimate new anonymous viewer out for 30 days

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:116 — Once the limit is reached, updateDevice matches only on the device_id the client sends, so anyone who reuses or guesses an active device ID gets past the limit and overwrites that device's IP and user agent

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:109 — The count check and the insert are separate statements with no lock, so concurrent requests with new device IDs can push the device count above device_limit

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44 — Device tagging now runs synchronously in the unauthenticated auth path with a COUNT(*) plus a write for every device ID not already cached, so floods of random IDs add DB load and slow down every anonymous request

pkg/api/frontendsettings.go:198 — anonymousDeviceLimit goes out in the frontend settings DTO, which unauthenticated clients also receive, revealing server licensing and capacity configuration that the frontend does not need

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database_test.go:69 — TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only asserts rejection of a new device, so it would still pass if updateDevice always returned ErrDeviceLimitReached; there is no test that an existing device can still be updated once the limit is reached.

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:95 — The at-limit update path treats rowsAffected==0 as limit reached, but on MySQL (default found-rows off) an update that writes identical values within the same second reports 0 rows, and no existing-device-at-limit test runs against the MySQL integration DB to catch this.

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44 — Authenticate now tags synchronously and fails auth on ErrDeviceLimitReached, yet no client test covers the rejection or confirms that other TagDevice errors are only logged.

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:87 — The local cache key is set before CreateOrUpdateDevice, so a device rejected for the limit gets a cache hit (nil error) on its next request and is let in; a TagDevice test that calls twice with limit>0 would catch this, but impl_test only uses limit 0.

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database_test.go:51 — No test covers the limit window edges: devices older than 30 days not counting toward the limit, updating an existing device whose updated_at is outside the 30-day window (it gets rejected), or limit=0 meaning unlimited.

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:43 — The service now builds its own AnonDBStore from db.DB, removing the injectable AnonStore seam, so service and client tests can't swap in a fake store to simulate ErrDeviceLimitReached and have to use a real DB.
pkg/setting/setting.go:1654 — Parsing of the new auth.anonymous device_limit key (and its default of 0) is not tested.

goldens.comment: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.

Anonymous authentication now fails entirely if anonDeviceService.TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Previously, device tagging was asynchronous and non-blocking. This change prevents anonymous users from authenticating when the device limit is reached.
The updateDevice function returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected == 0, but zero affected rows means the device doesn't exist or falls outside the time window, not that a limit was reached.

Time window calculation inconsistency: Using device.UpdatedAt.UTC().Add(-anonymousDeviceExpiration) as the lower bound but device.UpdatedAt as the current time may not match the intended logic. Consider using time.Now().UTC() consistently.

The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:115 — Device IDs come from a client-controlled header, so one unauthenticated client can send N random X-Grafana-Device-Id values to fill the limit and lock every new legitimate anonymous user out for up to 30 days (cascade DoS).

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:120 — Requests with no device-ID header (or an unparseable remote address) return nil before any limit check, so any API or script client that omits the header gets unlimited anonymous access and the limit only binds the cooperating frontend.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show the referenced impl.go logic (around line ~120) where requests without a device-ID header or with an unparseable RemoteAddr allegedly “return nil before any limit check.” In the shown changes, the device limit is enforced inside anonstore.CreateOrUpdateDevice and ErrDeviceLimitReached is propagated up through TagDevice (impl.go now returns the error) and Authenticate (client.go returns the error). Without the missing portion of TagDevice/ID extraction logic, the claimed bypass cannot be verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44 — Tagging now runs synchronously in Authenticate on the request context and adds a COUNT(*) plus a write on every cache miss, so a flood of unique device IDs turns into amplified DB load, and a slow DB directly adds latency to every new anonymous request.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes Authenticate() in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go from spawning a goroutine with a separate background timeout context to calling TagDevice(ctx, ...) synchronously on the request context. That means any DB latency in TagDevice now directly impacts anonymous request latency. Additionally, the new anonstore.CreateOrUpdateDevice logic (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go) performs a CountDevices(...) query before writing when deviceLimit > 0, so on each local-cache miss with device limit enabled you incur an extra COUNT(*) plus the upsert/write path. This is a concrete performance/architecture concern introduced by the change, though not a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database_test.go:51 — TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only checks that a new device is rejected; it never checks that an existing device can still update at the limit, or that a rejected device stays rejected on retry through TagDevice/cache, so the cache bypass passes green.

adjudication.rationale: The new device-limit logic in `CreateOrUpdateDevice` has two branches: when `count >= s.deviceLimit` it calls `s.updateDevice(ctx, device)` to allow updating an existing device within the expiration window, otherwise it inserts/upserts. `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` (added in this diff) only asserts that inserting a *different* `DeviceID` after reaching the limit returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`; it does not verify the intended behavior that an existing device can still be updated at the limit (the `updateDevice` path). The additional mention of retry behavior through `TagDevice`/local cache isn’t directly verified by this diff/test, but the core point about missing coverage for the update-at-limit branch is grounded in the changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:110 — The count-then-insert is not atomic (TOCTOU), so concurrent first requests from new devices across goroutines or HA instances can all see count < limit and insert, going past the configured limit.

pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:111 — If CountDevices fails (DB outage), the error is logged and authentication succeeds, and because the cache is already set that device skips enforcement for 29 minutes, so the limit fails open silently during DB degradation.

adjudication.rationale: In `AnonDBStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice`, a `CountDevices` DB error is returned (`if err != nil { return err }`). `AnonDeviceService.TagDevice` now propagates tagging errors (`return err`), but `Anonymous.Authenticate` only fails authentication for `ErrDeviceLimitReached`; any other error (including DB outages from `CountDevices`/writes) is merely logged and authentication continues. This means the new device-limit enforcement can fail open under DB degradation (tagging/limit checks fail, but anonymous auth still succeeds). The finding’s claim about cache timing isn’t shown in the diff, but the fail-open behavior is verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:52 — ProvideAnonDBStore gains an unbound int64 param and the AnonStore wire binding is no longer consumed, yet pkg/server/wire.go (and generated wire_gen/enterprise wireexts) are not updated in the diff, so the DI graph will fail to generate or leave a dangling provider.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `ProvideAnonDBStore` now requires a `deviceLimit int64` param, but it also changes `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` to take `sqlStore db.DB` and internally call `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore(sqlStore, cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit)`, and updates tests accordingly. The finding’s core claim—`pkg/server/wire.go` / generated wire files are not updated and DI will fail—cannot be verified from this diff because those files are not shown, and the change actually reduces the need to wire an `AnonStore` provider externally.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:37 — ProvideAnonymousDeviceService now takes db.DB and builds its store internally, which breaks any external caller or enterprise binding that injects anonstore.AnonStore and removes the ability to substitute the store.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService` changing its signature from accepting an injected `anonstore.AnonStore` to accepting a `db.DB` and constructing the store internally (`anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore(sqlStore, cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit)`). This concretely removes the ability for callers to substitute a different `AnonStore` implementation at construction time and is an API/DI design regression. The claim that it will break “external caller or enterprise binding” is plausible but not directly verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/setting/setting.go:1654 — New config key [auth.anonymous] device_limit is not added to conf/defaults.ini, conf/sample.ini, or the configuration docs, so operators cannot discover it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly adds reading of `auth.anonymous` key `device_limit` into `Cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit` (pkg/setting/setting.go), but it does not include any changes (or lack thereof) to `conf/defaults.ini`, `conf/sample.ini`, or documentation. Since those files are not present in the provided diff, the claim that the key was not added there cannot be verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:45 — Authenticate now returns a plain fmt.Errorf ErrDeviceLimitReached (not an errutil error), so anonymous clients over the limit get a generic auth failure with no stable status or message ID.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is defined as `fmt.Errorf("device limit reached")` in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go`, and `Authenticate` in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go` now returns that raw error when `TagDevice` hits the limit (`errors.Is(err, anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached) { return nil, err }`). However, the claimed impact about “generic auth failure with no stable status or message ID” depends on how upstream auth/error handling maps errors, which is not shown in this diff. So the concrete, diff-grounded issue is the use of an untyped/plain error for a control-flow/auth failure, but the exact response semantics can’t be verified here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/grafana-data/src/types/config.ts:200 — TS type declares anonymousDeviceLimit as number or undefined, but the Go DTO is a non-pointer int64 without omitempty, so the backend always sends a number (0 meaning unlimited) and undefined never occurs.

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows Go always populates/sends a concrete int64: `Cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit` is read via `MustInt64(0)`, `FrontendSettingsDTO.AnonymousDeviceLimit int64` has no `omitempty`, and `getFrontendSettings` assigns it directly, so JSON will always include a number (typically 0 when unset). Meanwhile TS declares `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined` and the boot config default is `undefined`, which is a type/contract mismatch (frontend may think `undefined` is possible even though this backend always emits a number). This is a typing/compatibility concern rather than a proven runtime defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/grafana-runtime/src/config.ts:97 — Without a type annotation, `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined` narrows the GrafanaBootConfig property to type undefined under strict mode, so consumers can't read it as a number.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/grafana-runtime/src/config.ts`, `GrafanaBootConfig` adds `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined;` with no type annotation. TypeScript will infer the class property type as `undefined`, which is narrower than the intended `number | undefined` added to `GrafanaConfig` in `packages/grafana-data/src/types/config.ts`. While this still structurally satisfies the interface, consumers using the concrete `GrafanaBootConfig` type (or any later assignment of a number to this field) will hit type errors because the property is inferred as `undefined` rather than `number | undefined`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:87 — Device key is cached before CreateOrUpdateDevice runs, so after a new device gets ErrDeviceLimitReached, its next requests within 29 minutes hit the cache, TagDevice returns nil, and anonymous auth succeeds, bypassing the limit

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a device limit error path (anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached) and changes TagDevice to return an error when tagDeviceUI fails (impl.go now `return err`). The finding hinges on specific behavior/order inside TagDevice/tagDeviceUI (caching the device key *before* CreateOrUpdateDevice and then returning nil on later cached requests), but that caching logic/order is not shown in the provided diff. From what is shown, an ErrDeviceLimitReached would propagate up (and in client.go would abort auth), not be silently bypassed. Therefore the claimed bypass cannot be verified from this diff alone.

This makes authentication latency depend on the TagDevice path. In `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go`, when `deviceLimit > 0`, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` performs a `CountDevices` query and may then `UPDATE`; when `deviceLimit == 0`, it skips the count but still performs the upsert/insert, so there is still at least one DB round-trip on cache misses. This is a real, diff-grounded performance/architecture concern (auth path now blocks on DB work), but not a clear functional correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:87 — Cache key is set before CreateOrUpdateDevice, so after a device is rejected with ErrDeviceLimitReached every later request within 29m hits the cache, returns nil, and authenticates, making the limit enforceable only on the first request

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show the TagDevice (impl.go) cache-key set/lookup logic around CreateOrUpdateDevice, so the claimed sequence (“cache key is set before CreateOrUpdateDevice”, then ErrDeviceLimitReached, then later requests hit cache and return nil) cannot be verified from the provided changes. What is visible is that TagDevice now returns the error from tagDeviceUI, and client.Authenticate now propagates anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached instead of logging asynchronously, which tends to enforce the limit rather than bypass it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:87 — Now that the write uses the request ctx, a client disconnect or transient DB error leaves the device unrecorded while the pre-set cache entry suppresses any retry for 29m, undercounting devices

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a behavior change: in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go` the tagging call is no longer done in a goroutine with `context.Background()` + timeout; it now calls `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...)` using the request context. That makes tagging sensitive to client disconnect / request cancellation and transient failures, which can lead to devices not being recorded. The service also maintains a long-lived local cache (`localcache.New(29*time.Minute, ...)` in `ProvideAnonymousDeviceService`), so if cache entries are set before a successful DB write (not shown in the provided diff), this could suppress retries for ~29 minutes. However, the diff snippet does not include the cache-set logic/order, so the “pre-set cache entry suppresses retry” part cannot be directly verified here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44 — Tagging now runs synchronously in Authenticate with the request ctx and no timeout (the old 2m bounded detached ctx is gone), so a slow or unavailable DB adds COUNT+write latency or stalls anonymous requests

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go, the previous async goroutine with a detached context and 2-minute timeout (timeoutTag + context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), ...)) was removed. Authenticate now directly calls a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...) synchronously. Since TagDevice can hit the DB (and now may also do CountDevices + update/insert via anonstore), a slow/unavailable DB can delay or stall the anonymous Authenticate path until the request ctx is canceled. This is a real diff-grounded latency/availability concern, but not a clearly verifiable functional correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:110 — Count-then-insert is not atomic (no transaction/lock), so concurrent new devices across requests/instances can each see count<limit and exceed the configured device limit

adjudication.rationale: In `CreateOrUpdateDevice` (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go), the limit enforcement is implemented as `CountDevices(...)` followed by an insert/upsert when `count < s.deviceLimit`. There is no transaction, lock, or DB constraint tying the count check to the subsequent insert/update, so concurrent requests (or multiple instances) can both observe `count < limit` and proceed to create new devices, exceeding `deviceLimit`. The diff shows no atomicity mechanism around this sequence.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:95 — rowsAffected==0 is treated as limit reached, but MySQL reports 0 affected rows when the UPDATE changes nothing (same-second updated_at, same IP/UA), so a legitimately registered device can be rejected

adjudication.rationale: In anonstore/database.go `updateDevice` treats `rowsAffected == 0` as `ErrDeviceLimitReached` after an `UPDATE anon_device SET client_ip=?, user_agent=?, updated_at=? ...` (new code around the added `updateDevice` function). When the device exists but the new values equal the stored values (notably `updated_at` can be identical if the DB column has coarse time resolution), some DBs (e.g., MySQL) can return 0 affected rows even though a matching row was found. This would incorrectly surface `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, and in anonimpl/client.go that error is now returned from `Authenticate`, potentially rejecting a legitimate existing device once the limit is reached.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:87 — Device key is cached before CreateOrUpdateDevice runs, so after an ErrDeviceLimitReached rejection the same device ID gets through on any retry within 29 minutes (cache hit returns nil), which means the limit only blocks the first request

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show the ordering of local-cache writes vs the DB call in `AnonDeviceService.TagDevice` (the code around the alleged `impl.go:87` cache set is not included). While the service clearly has a `localCache` and `TagDevice` now propagates errors from `tagDeviceUI` (including `ErrDeviceLimitReached`), nothing in the shown changes verifies that a device key is cached *before* `CreateOrUpdateDevice` runs, nor that a cache hit causes `TagDevice` to return `nil` after a previous `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. This finding depends on unseen code, so it cannot be confirmed from the provided diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:120 — A request that leaves out the client-controlled X-Grafana-Device-Id header, or has an unparseable remote address (line 128), returns nil before the limit check and still gets anonymous access, so curl or API clients bypass the device limit completely

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show the referenced logic in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go` around “line 120/128” (e.g., early `return nil` when `X-Grafana-Device-Id` is missing or when `RemoteAddr` is unparseable). The only shown change in `TagDevice` is that it now returns `err` if `tagDeviceUI` fails. The device-limit logic is implemented in `anonstore.CreateOrUpdateDevice` and is only triggered when a device record is being created/updated; the diff alone does not demonstrate that missing headers or bad `RemoteAddr` causes an early return that bypasses the limit while still granting access.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:115 — An unauthenticated attacker can send requests with random device IDs (no rate limiting or verification) to fill device_limit, locking every legitimate new anonymous viewer out for 30 days

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an enforcement path where, once `deviceLimit` is reached, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` stops inserting and calls `updateDevice`; if the `device_id` doesn’t already exist, the UPDATE affects 0 rows and returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` (see `updateDevice` and the `count >= s.deviceLimit` branch). The anonymous auth flow now calls `TagDevice` synchronously and returns the error for `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, denying authentication (`client.go`). Since new device IDs are inserted up to the limit with no checks shown in this diff, a client sending many distinct device IDs can fill the limit and cause subsequent new devices to be rejected for the 30-day window used in counting (`anonymousDeviceExpiration`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:116 — Once the limit is reached, updateDevice matches only on the device_id the client sends, so anyone who reuses or guesses an active device ID gets past the limit and overwrites that device's IP and user agent

adjudication.rationale: In the new limit path, CreateOrUpdateDevice() calls updateDevice() when count >= deviceLimit. updateDevice() performs an UPDATE keyed only by the caller-supplied device_id (plus an updated_at time window): `WHERE device_id = ? AND updated_at BETWEEN ? AND ?`, and if it affects a row it will overwrite `client_ip`, `user_agent`, and `updated_at`. This means a client that can supply/reuse a valid (recent) device_id can avoid ErrDeviceLimitReached and be “accepted” under the limit logic while also clobbering that device’s metadata. That behavior is directly implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:109 — The count check and the insert are separate statements with no lock, so concurrent requests with new device IDs can push the device count above device_limit

adjudication.rationale: In `CreateOrUpdateDevice` (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go), the limit enforcement does a `CountDevices(...)` check and then proceeds to an upsert/insert path when `count < s.deviceLimit`. These are separate DB operations with no transaction/locking shown in the diff. Under concurrent requests for different new `DeviceID`s, multiple goroutines can observe the same count below the limit and both insert, causing the number of rows in the 30-day window to exceed `deviceLimit`. The `updateDevice` fallback only triggers when the count is already at/above the limit, so it does not prevent this race.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44 — Device tagging now runs synchronously in the unauthenticated auth path with a COUNT(*) plus a write for every device ID not already cached, so floods of random IDs add DB load and slow down every anonymous request

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Anonymous.Authenticate` from launching device tagging in a goroutine with a background timeout to calling `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...)` inline (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go), so tagging DB work can now add latency to the anonymous auth path. Additionally, when `cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit > 0`, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` performs a `CountDevices(...)` before the upsert and may then run an `UPDATE` (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go), increasing per-request DB load under that configuration. The finding overstates it slightly because the COUNT only happens when the limit is enabled (default is 0), and the cache behavior isn’t shown here, but the synchronous-on-request-path performance/abuse concern is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/frontendsettings.go:198 — anonymousDeviceLimit goes out in the frontend settings DTO, which unauthenticated clients also receive, revealing server licensing and capacity configuration that the frontend does not need

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `AnonymousDeviceLimit` to `FrontendSettingsDTO` (`pkg/api/dtos/frontend_settings.go`) and populates it from server config in `getFrontendSettings` (`pkg/api/frontendsettings.go`), so the value is indeed sent to the frontend. However, the claim that this is received by *unauthenticated* clients and that it reveals “licensing” cannot be verified from the diff (no route/auth context shown, and the field is a generic limit). Still, it’s a concrete, diff-grounded concern about potentially exposing an internal capacity/security-related configuration via frontend settings if the frontend doesn’t strictly need it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database_test.go:69 — TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only asserts rejection of a new device, so it would still pass if updateDevice always returned ErrDeviceLimitReached; there is no test that an existing device can still be updated once the limit is reached.

adjudication.rationale: In `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit`, after filling the limit with the first insert, the test changes `DeviceID` to a new value (`"keep"`) and expects `ErrDeviceLimitReached` on the second `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. That only exercises the "limit reached + update of non-existent device" path, because `updateDevice` will `UPDATE ... WHERE device_id = ?` and affect 0 rows, returning `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. There is no assertion that an *existing* device can still be updated once `count >= deviceLimit`, so the test would indeed still pass even if `updateDevice` always returned `ErrDeviceLimitReached`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:95 — The at-limit update path treats rowsAffected==0 as limit reached, but on MySQL (default found-rows off) an update that writes identical values within the same second reports 0 rows, and no existing-device-at-limit test runs against the MySQL integration DB to catch this.

adjudication.rationale: In `updateDevice` (new in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go`), the code treats `rowsAffected == 0` as `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. But `rowsAffected==0` can also occur when the row *matched* the `WHERE device_id = ? AND updated_at BETWEEN ? AND ?` predicate yet the `SET` writes identical values (notably on MySQL, which commonly reports 0 affected rows when no actual data changes). That would incorrectly fail updating an existing device once the limit is reached, returning a limit error even though the device exists. The added test `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only exercises the non-existing-device update-at-limit path (different `DeviceID`), and does not cover updating an existing device at the limit to catch this behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44 — Authenticate now tags synchronously and fails auth on ErrDeviceLimitReached, yet no client test covers the rejection or confirms that other TagDevice errors are only logged.
matched_golden_ids: Anonymous authentication now fails entirely if anonDeviceService.TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Previously, device tagging was asynchronous and non-blocking. This change prevents anonymous users from authenticating when the device limit is reached.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that anonymous Authenticate now performs device tagging synchronously and rejects authentication when TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, which matches the golden concern that anon auth is now blocked by device-limit errors (previously non-blocking/asynchronous). The added note about missing tests is extra but not conflicting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:87 — The local cache key is set before CreateOrUpdateDevice, so a device rejected for the limit gets a cache hit (nil error) on its next request and is let in; a TagDevice test that calls twice with limit>0 would catch this, but impl_test only uses limit 0.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly introduces a new rejection path via `anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached` (e.g., `AnonDBStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice` returning it when `count >= s.deviceLimit`) and then propagates it up (`TagDevice` now returns the error; `Anonymous.Authenticate` denies login only when `errors.Is(err, anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached)`). However, the specific claim that the local cache key is set *before* `CreateOrUpdateDevice` (causing a later cache hit to bypass the limit) is not shown in the provided diff hunks, so that exact defect can’t be verified here. What is verifiable is that `impl_test.go` uses `setting.NewCfg()` (thus `AnonymousDeviceLimit` defaulting to 0) and adds no service-level test exercising the new limit/error propagation behavior, which is a concrete gap for newly added nontrivial logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database_test.go:51 — No test covers the limit window edges: devices older than 30 days not counting toward the limit, updating an existing device whose updated_at is outside the 30-day window (it gets rejected), or limit=0 meaning unlimited.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial device-limit logic with a 30-day window (`anonymousDeviceExpiration`) in `CreateOrUpdateDevice` and `updateDevice` (counting devices in a time range and only allowing updates when `updated_at BETWEEN updatedAt-30d AND updatedAt+1m`, otherwise returning `ErrDeviceLimitReached`). The new test `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` only covers the simple “limit reached + inserting a new device ID” path and does not cover the stated edge cases (excluding devices older than 30 days from the count, behavior when updating an existing device whose stored `updated_at` is outside the 30-day window, or explicitly asserting that `deviceLimit=0` disables the limit). Those gaps are specific to the newly introduced time-windowed limit behavior, but they are missing tests rather than a proven defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:43 — The service now builds its own AnonDBStore from db.DB, removing the injectable AnonStore seam, so service and client tests can't swap in a fake store to simulate ErrDeviceLimitReached and have to use a real DB.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows ProvideAnonymousDeviceService no longer accepts an anonstore.AnonStore; it now takes a db.DB and internally constructs the store via anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore(sqlStore, cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit) (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go). This removes the injection seam for tests to supply a fake AnonStore (including one that forces ErrDeviceLimitReached) and pushes tests toward using a real DB-backed store, as reflected by test changes (impl_test.go now passes store and inspects anonService.anonStore). This is a testability/architecture regression rather than a runtime correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/setting/setting.go:1654 — Parsing of the new auth.anonymous device_limit key (and its default of 0) is not tested.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds parsing of `auth.anonymous` `device_limit` via `cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit = anonSection.Key("device_limit").MustInt64(0)` in `readAuthSettings` (pkg/setting/setting.go), but this PR diff does not add or adjust any tests that cover this new INI key or its default value of 0. That’s a concrete, diff-grounded test gap rather than a functional defect shown in the code.
